title: Strengthening Regulatory Regime for Nursing Homes
what_it_is: Strengthening Regulatory Regime for Nursing Homes

sections.label: Nursing home licence revocations
sections.summary: Most nursing homes on closer monitoring correct lapses, but serious repeated gaps lead MOH to escalate measures, as in two licence revocations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The great majority of nursing homes placed on closer monitoring take adequate corrective actions and sustain the improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, if the gaps are serious, repeated and there is a lack of serious effort to rectify them, such as in the case of Windsor Convalescent Home and LC Nursing Home, MOH will have to escalate our measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These two cases of licence revocation are therefore an outcome of the regulatory framework working as intended.

sections.label: Revoked licences and Vanguard takeover
sections.summary: MOH revoked two operators' licences when remediation was inadequate and arranged for Vanguard Healthcare to step in.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: When we ascertained that the remediation efforts were inadequate or were not sustained for the two operators, we revoked their licences and arranged for Vanguard Healthcare to step in.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH and the Agency for Integrated Care will also be sharing the findings of our recent audits, and the various manpower training and grant support available with the nursing home sector.

sections.label: MOH regulatory framework and limits
sections.summary: MOH's framework assesses licensees' compliance with the Healthcare Services Act, but MOH cannot coordinate private claims against nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH's regulatory framework aims at assessing licensees' care delivery practices and protocols in compliance with the Healthcare Services Act to ensure resident safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: When necessary, we will step in and take over the operations or coordinate the relocation of residents to another facility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, as the provision of care is a contract between the resident and the nursing home, MOH is unable to coordinate private claims from residents or their families against the nursing home.

sections.label: Informing families of rectification
sections.summary: MOH's first priority in informing family members is ensuring improvements are done and residents' safety is not endangered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Thirdly, on informing the family members, MOH's first priority is to make sure those improvements are done, lapses are rectified and to make sure nothing endangers the residents' safety.
